newsitem.title: PERU: Peruvians pessimistic over end to hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: Peruvians pessimistic over end to hostage crisis.

text.p: More than half of Peruvians believe the 90-day Lima hostage crisis will take at least one more month to resolve, a leading pollster said on Monday.

Apoyo S.A., the country's leading polling firm, said 33 percent of 500 people surveyed believed the crisis would last another one to three months, while 20 percent thought it would take more than three months.
Only 14 percent believed the standoff between the Peruvian government and Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels would be over within a month.

The Marxist rebels stormed a cocktail party at the Japanese ambassador's residence on Dec. 17 and are holding 72 captives to demand the release of some 400 jailed MRTA members. Face-to-face talks seem to have done little to hasten a solution as the crisis completed its third month on Monday.

The Apoyo poll said 46 percent believed the MRTA's accusation that the government had built a tunnel underneath the residence in preparation for a possible assault. Only 35 percent did not accept that version.
President Alberto Fujimori's personal approval rating was 52 percent in March, up from 46 percent the previous month, in an apparent reflection of public backing for his tough handling of the crisis.

But the poll showed the twice-elected president was no shoe-in if he runs for office again in 2000. If voting were held tomorrow, 40 percent of people would cast their ballot for Lima's popular mayor Alberto Andrade as president, compared to 37 percent for Fujimori.
The Apoyo poll had a 4.5 percent margin of error.
